justification: The run comprehensively added hosted openings across all three occupied floors: 100 doors and 98 windows, with every one of the 91 rooms having at least one door and the perimeter occupied rooms generally receiving exterior glazing. However, the repeated lift-threshold defects across every floor, plus an inappropriate full-height internal window between a toilet and staff lounge, require substantial opening-specific rework and keep this from being an acceptably finished package.
evidence: Live measurements found 40/32 doors/windows on L1, 30/36 on L2, and 30/30 on L3; all 198 openings have wall hosts. The opening measurements report 12 Major lift-door findings, including a 1.00 m swing door rather than a ≥1.20 m sliding lift landing door. One window is a 1.813 m-wide fixed window with a 0.594 m sill between “L3 Researcher toilet room” and “L3 Staff lounge and pantry.” The agent acknowledged unresolved work: “Model check: 21 findings are still open, all about the lifts.”
strengths: Whole-building coverage was delivered: all three occupied storeys contain substantial door and window sets.

The access check found no rooms without doors: 31 rooms are reachable on L1 and the 60 upper-floor rooms are internally connected but reported not linked to other floors only because the disclosed reserved cores contain no physical vertical equipment, which is not penalized here.
All 198 openings returned a wall host; no unhosted opening was found.
Door bases align with their floor levels on all three storeys, and window heads and sills follow a consistent three-type system.

Habitable perimeter uses such as study rooms, offices, reading rooms, collections, workrooms, meeting rooms and the staff lounge generally have exterior windows; intentionally dark archive and special-collection stores were appropriately left blind.

The opening measurements found no hinge-return defects or inward-opening operable sashes; most ordinary room doors open into their rooms, while the reading hall and reserved stair/plant uses use appropriate outward exceptions.
Toilet exterior windows are consistently high-level, approximately 1.794 m sill with 0.613 m height.
weaknesses: Twelve Major lift-door findings repeat across all three floors. Passenger and service lift reservations open directly onto galleries rather than lift lobbies; the southeast goods-lift thresholds also use double-swing or 1.00 m swing doors instead of suitable ≥1.20 m sliding landing doors.
One window creates an unsuitable low-sill, nearly full-height transparent opening directly between the L3 Researcher toilet room and Staff lounge and pantry, compromising toilet privacy.
The agent stopped with known lift-opening problems instead of resolving them, despite the generic brief requiring a coherent completed opening scheme.
Moving-leaf and sash sweep clearance could not be established from the opening measurements and is therefore not assessed.
The interim statement “All 100 doors and 130 windows are in” was incorrect for the delivered model, although the final response corrected the count to 98 windows.

spec_violations.constraint: Lift landing doors must slide, be at least 1.20 m wide, and open onto a lift lobby.
spec_violations.what_happened: Lift reservations open directly onto galleries throughout the building, and the southeast goods-lift thresholds include swinging and undersized doors.
spec_violations.evidence: Opening measurements list 12 Major lift-door findings across storeys 1–3; three of them are 1.00 m swing doors.

spec_violations.constraint: Openings must preserve privacy and use a family suitable for the room.
spec_violations.what_happened: A large low-sill fixed window connects a researcher toilet directly to a staff lounge/pantry.
spec_violations.evidence: The window: fixed operation, 1.813 m nominal width, 0.594 m sill, sides “L3 Researcher toilet room” and “L3 Staff lounge and pantry”.
